why_now.business_demand: Marketing agencies, social content studios and design teams need junior motion designers who can animate logos, titles, infographics and kinetic type with high craft.
why_now.career_opportunity: Foundational 2D motion design bridges graphic design into the high-demand field of commercial motion graphics and digital visual production.

skill_boundaries.course_focus: Course 72 is an accessible, beginner-to-applied certification in 2D motion design, After Effects animation fundamentals, shape motion and kinetic typography.
skill_boundaries.course_69_differentiation: Course 69 (Adobe After Effects — Motion Design & Compositing) is a comprehensive post-production specialization covering advanced Graph Editor curves, 3D camera tracking, Mocha planar tracking, green-screen compositing, rotoscoping, complex expressions, and reusable commercial MOGRT / Essential Properties engineering.
skill_boundaries.progression_path: Course 72 serves as the ideal foundational prerequisite before progressing to advanced compositing and motion systems in Course 69.

Advanced procedural motion rigs and physics simulations
Professional mocha planar tracking and camera solve tracking

Character rigging with Duik or advanced bone hierarchies
High-end broadcast MOGRT template systems with master properties scripting

modules.module_purpose: Understand how design elements move, how motion communicates meaning and how professional animation uses timing, spacing and visual hierarchy.

lessons.what_is_taught: Foundations of 2D motion graphics: distinguishing motion design from video editing and visual effects, common commercial applications across brand identity, digital advertising, educational content, UI motion and social media animation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Deconstructs commercial motion graphics examples to identify communicative objectives versus visual ornamentation.
lessons.why_it_matters: Motion graphics exist to clarify communication, not simply add moving decorative elements.
lessons.expected_outcome: Clear grasp of motion design's commercial role, terminology and production scope.

lessons.what_is_taught: Essential visual design principles applied to motion: vector shapes, colour theory and contrast, typography hierarchy, grid alignment, compositional balance, white space management, and visual focus zones.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a static design composition optimized for subsequent animation with intentional focal hierarchy.
lessons.why_it_matters: Flawed static compositions produce confusing animations; solid design must precede movement.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to construct clean, well-balanced graphic compositions ready for animation.

lessons.what_is_taught: Core animation principles translated for graphic motion: timing and spacing, anticipation, follow-through, overlapping action, ease-in and ease-out, rhythm, visual continuity, and subtle squash and stretch awareness.
lessons.what_learner_does: Sketches motion pathways and spacing charts for graphic elements transitioning across screen.
lessons.why_it_matters: Without animation principles, digital movement feels robotic, harsh and amateur.
lessons.expected_outcome: Theoretical and visual mastery of foundational motion principles.

lessons.what_is_taught: The mechanics of time: frame rates (24fps, 30fps, 60fps), animation durations, frame intervals versus real-world seconds, fast versus slow motion psychology, linear intervals, and natural physical acceleration.
lessons.what_learner_does: Tests identical graphic moves across varying frame intervals to observe perceptual differences.
lessons.why_it_matters: Accurate timing determines whether motion feels snappy, weighted, graceful or lethargic.
lessons.expected_outcome: Precise temporal judgment for pacing graphic transitions.

lessons.what_is_taught: Why linear computer movement appears artificial and robotic; understanding Ease In, Ease Out, Easy Ease, speed curves, movement velocity transitions, and intentional cases for constant mechanical motion.
lessons.what_learner_does: Compares linear motion to eased keyframes on simple geometric shapes to calibrate visual smoothness.
lessons.why_it_matters: Easing is the single most critical factor separating amateur timeline work from professional motion craft.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to apply appropriate easing profiles to basic property animations.

lessons.what_is_taught: Guiding the viewer's eye: primary motion versus secondary accents, establishing clear visual focal points, layered animation sequencing, and avoiding competing simultaneous movements.
lessons.what_learner_does: Plans an animation sequence where elements arrive in clear hierarchical order to direct viewer gaze.
lessons.why_it_matters: When everything moves at the same time, the viewer sees nothing and the message is lost.
lessons.expected_outcome: Competence in staging layered animations with unmistakable visual priorities.

lessons.what_is_taught: Designing type that moves without sacrificing readability: font weight selection, contrast against backgrounds, word count considerations, required screen reading times, safe margins, and message-driven pacing.
lessons.what_learner_does: Calculates required reading duration for a 10-word sentence and plans entrance and hold durations.
lessons.why_it_matters: If viewers cannot comfortably read the text, the motion graphic fails its primary business objective.
lessons.expected_outcome: Knowledge of typographic legibility rules under temporal constraints.

lessons.what_is_taught: Analyzing professional motion design critically: dissecting timing, recognizing transition techniques, building reference boards, reverse-engineering easing curves, and distinguishing inspirational reference from direct imitation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conducts a frame-by-frame breakdown of an award-winning brand reveal, recording keyframe timings.
lessons.why_it_matters: Developing an analytical eye allows self-directed learning and higher aesthetic standards.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to audit professional animations and extract applicable motion techniques.

lessons.what_is_taught: Pre-production methodology for motion projects: interpreting creative briefs, defining core messages and target audiences, creating thumbnail storyboards, designing style frames, and mapping motion direction and audio cues.
lessons.what_learner_does: Drafts a 4-panel storyboard and visual style reference sheet for a branded promotional sequence.
lessons.why_it_matters: Planning before keyframing saves hours of wasted timeline rework and client misunderstandings.
lessons.expected_outcome: Creation of a structured motion brief and storyboard ready for After Effects production.

modules.module_purpose: Develop practical proficiency with Adobe After Effects and create original keyframed animations using transforms, easing, parenting and masks.

lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating the After Effects workspace: Project panel, Composition viewer, Timeline panel, Properties inspector, Preview controls, Effects & Presets library, workspace customization, and high-frequency keyboard shortcuts.
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures a streamlined workspace layout and navigates panels using standard keyboard shortcuts.
lessons.why_it_matters: Fluency with the interface reduces friction and speeds up iterative timeline adjustments.
lessons.expected_outcome: Confident navigation and efficient operation inside the After Effects environment.

lessons.what_is_taught: Creating and configuring compositions: resolution standards (1080p, 4K), frame rate selection (24fps vs 30fps), timeline duration, pixel aspect ratio, background color, naming conventions, and standard aspect ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1).
lessons.what_learner_does: Sets up standard 1080x1920 (vertical 9:16) and 1920x1080 (horizontal 16:9) master compositions with correct frame rates.
lessons.why_it_matters: Incorrect composition settings lead to blurry exports, distorted pixels and delivery rejections.
lessons.expected_outcome: Correct technical composition setup matching professional broadcast and web specifications.

lessons.what_is_taught: Understanding timeline layer types: Shape layers, Text layers, Solid layers, imported image assets, layer stacking order, in-points and out-points, layer visibility switches, solo switches, locking, and systematic layer naming.
lessons.what_learner_does: Imports multi-layer vector assets, organizes layers into stacking order, and trims durations cleanly.
lessons.why_it_matters: Unorganized layers with default names create confusion and slow down revisions in multi-element comps.
lessons.expected_outcome: Disciplined layer management and clean timeline hierarchy.

lessons.what_is_taught: The core transform properties of every visual layer: Anchor Point (A), Position (P), Scale (S), Rotation (R), and Opacity (T); understanding their mathematical relationships, coordinate axes (X, Y), and simultaneous animation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates basic shapes across all five transform properties to master keyboard shortcuts and value adjustments.
lessons.why_it_matters: All 2D animation builds directly upon mastering these fundamental transform properties.
lessons.expected_outcome: Intuitive command over all five basic transform properties.

lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering the anchor point: how anchor point position dictates the center of rotation and scale origin, using the Pan Behind (Anchor Point) tool, snapping anchor points to corners/centers, and troubleshooting common beginner scaling errors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Repositions anchor points to layer corners and edges to animate rotating doors, growing bars, and pendulum swings.
lessons.why_it_matters: Misplaced anchor points result in unnatural rotations and shapes scaling from the wrong origin.
lessons.expected_outcome: Flawless placement and repositioning of layer anchor points.

lessons.what_is_taught: The mechanics of keyframing: enabling stopwatch controls, inserting keyframes, selecting and repositioning keyframes on timeline, copying and pasting keyframes, modifying property values, and real-time playback previews.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a sequential animation of an icon entering, hovering, and exiting using manual keyframe placement.
lessons.why_it_matters: Keyframes are the atomic unit of digital animation; precision here dictates the final motion quality.
lessons.expected_outcome: Precise keyframing skills without unintentional keyframe duplication.

lessons.what_is_taught: Transforming stiff keyframes into natural motion: applying Easy Ease (F9), Ease In (Shift+F9), and Ease Out (Ctrl+Shift+F9); introduction to the Graph Editor, viewing speed graphs, and visually inspecting velocity handles.
lessons.what_learner_does: Opens the Graph Editor and shapes the speed curve of a sliding panel from sharp linear to a graceful ease-out curve.
lessons.why_it_matters: Basic curve shaping produces polished, commercially acceptable motion dynamics.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to manipulate basic speed graph curves to achieve refined easing.

lessons.what_is_taught: Establishing parent-child relationships between layers: using the pickwhip tool, parenting menus, inheriting transform properties (position, scale, rotation), and introducing Null Objects as master animation controllers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Parents multiple graphic sub-elements to a Null Object to orchestrate unified group movement.
lessons.why_it_matters: Parenting prevents keyframing dozens of individual layers independently, keeping projects editable.
lessons.expected_outcome: Effective use of parenting and null objects to streamline coordinated motion.

lessons.what_is_taught: Creating and using layer masks: rectangle and pen tool masks, mask expansion, mask feathering, animating mask paths for linear reveals, and distinguishing layer masks from vector shape layers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates an inverted mask path to create a clean, graphic wipe reveal of a product photograph.
lessons.why_it_matters: Masking provides clean boundaries and reveal transitions essential for commercial motion design.
lessons.expected_outcome: Proficiency in creating, animating and feathering layer masks.

lessons.what_is_taught: Professional project hygiene: folder structure in Project panel (Compositions, Assets, Audio, Solids), consistent layer color-coding, saving incremental project versions, handling missing asset links, and basic timeline troubleshooting.
lessons.what_learner_does: Organizes a messy After Effects project into clean standard folders and prepares it for archivals.
lessons.why_it_matters: Cluttered projects confuse collaborators, cause lost work and fail professional handover standards.
lessons.expected_outcome: Impeccable project organization and asset management habits.

modules.module_purpose: Create original vector-based motion graphics using shape layers, Trim Paths, coordinated movement and meaningful geometric transitions.

lessons.what_is_taught: Building vectors directly inside After Effects: parametric shapes (rectangles, ellipses, polygons), custom pen paths, fill types (solid, gradient), stroke properties (line caps, joins, dashes), shape groups, and internal layer transform controls.
lessons.what_learner_does: Draws and styles a custom vector badge using multiple shape groups and styled strokes within a single layer.
lessons.why_it_matters: Shape layers render infinitely crisp vector lines at any scale and unlock dedicated shape animators.
lessons.expected_outcome: Comprehensive understanding of shape layer properties and internal group architecture.

lessons.what_is_taught: Animating shape-specific attributes: path morphing awareness, animated corner rounding, stroke width modulation, dynamic fill colour transitions, and animating multiple shape groups within a unified coordinate system.
subtopics: Colour transitions in fills and strokes
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates an alert icon transitioning from a circle into an active checkmark through path and stroke transforms.
lessons.why_it_matters: Animating shape attributes directly enables sleek UI and infographic icon animations.
lessons.expected_outcome: Skill in animating shape-specific properties beyond standard transform keys.

lessons.what_is_taught: The Trim Paths operator: Start, End, and Offset properties; animating line draws, circular progress indicators, decorative stroke flourishes, and revealing logo vector outlines smoothly.
subtopics: Adding Trim Paths to shape layers
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a circular data gauge that animates from 0% to 85% with an offset animated decorative stroke.
lessons.why_it_matters: Trim Paths is the most versatile and widely used vector animation technique in commercial motion graphics.
lessons.expected_outcome: Complete command of Trim Paths for lines, rings and vector reveals.

lessons.what_is_taught: Designing coherent movement systems: establishing consistent directional momentum, repeating geometric motifs, balancing primary and supporting shape accents, and maintaining visual rhythm across multiple animated objects.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a 3-element geometric motion system where shapes move with synchronized rhythm and directional harmony.
lessons.why_it_matters: Random uncoordinated movements look chaotic; consistent movement systems feel branded and intentional.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to construct unified, harmonious multi-element shape animations.

lessons.what_is_taught: Creating visual depth through staggered timing: offsetting keyframes by frames, sequential entrances, cascade reveals, grouping animation timelines, and avoiding identical simultaneous arrivals.
lessons.what_learner_does: Staggers the arrival of 5 infographic bar charts by 3-frame increments to create an energetic cascade reveal.
lessons.why_it_matters: Temporal staggering adds organic fluidity and makes complex data easy for viewers to process.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluency in staggering layers and keyframes for natural, layered reveals.

lessons.what_is_taught: Constructing original scene transitions using shape layers: full-screen shape wipes, expanding circle reveals, linear diagonal slices, scale-burst transitions, directional motion cuts, and maintaining visual continuity across scene changes.
subtopics: Matching cut points on peak coverage
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a 2-second geometric transition that wipes the screen cleanly to reveal a second scene with seamless continuity.
lessons.why_it_matters: Original transitions create fluid scene handoffs without resorting to generic crossfades or plugin presets.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to design and execute clean, original geometric transitions.

lessons.what_is_taught: Building seamless repeating animations: matching first and last frame states, calculating loop durations, cyclical movement paths, rotational loops, and introductory loop expression awareness (e.g. loopOut) without complex code.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a 3-second seamless looping animated graphic suitable for web banners and social feeds.
lessons.why_it_matters: Seamless loops are essential for digital signage, web UI animations, and repeating social media stickers.
lessons.expected_outcome: Competence in building smooth, perfectly looping 2D animations.

lessons.what_is_taught: Polishing motion in the Graph Editor: refining influence handles, smoothing velocity transitions, applying appropriate motion blur, avoiding erratic acceleration spikes, and balancing snappy movement with visual clarity.
lessons.what_learner_does: Refines a geometric animation's curves so that all components decelerate and settle with synchronized ease.
lessons.why_it_matters: Subtle velocity curve polish separates mediocre beginner work from professional client-ready motion.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to fine-tune speed graphs for polished, cohesive movement.

lessons.what_is_taught: Applying vector shape motion in commercial contexts: animated icons for websites and apps, motion infographics, product feature callout pointers, branded accent flourishes, and social video stickers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs and animates an infographic card featuring an animated statistic, callout line and data icon.
lessons.why_it_matters: These commercial deliverables form the everyday workload of junior motion designers and creative studios.
lessons.expected_outcome: Practical portfolio skills in producing commercially relevant shape animations.

lessons.what_is_taught: Systematic quality control: checking animation smoothness, verifying frame-accurate timing, pixel-perfect vector alignment, consistent movement vectors, eliminating visual flicker, and checking alpha transparency channels.
lessons.what_learner_does: Performs a 6-point quality assurance check on an animated sequence, correcting timing hitches and edge artifacts.
lessons.why_it_matters: QA ensures student work meets professional agency standards before presentation or handover.
lessons.expected_outcome: Disciplined review habits ensuring technical and visual excellence.

modules.module_purpose: Use animation to bring text, brand identity and marketing communication to life using text animators, logo reveals and reusable title systems.

lessons.what_is_taught: Foundations of motion typography: selecting legible display and body typefaces, managing line height and kerning for motion, contrast against background video/graphics, safe text boundaries, and aligning typographic choices with brand personality.
subtopics: Safe margins and Title Safe zones
lessons.what_learner_does: Selects and formats a typographic hierarchy for a motion piece, verifying contrast and screen-safe placement.
lessons.why_it_matters: Good animated typography requires sound typographic fundamentals; poor font choices undermine motion quality.
lessons.expected_outcome: Solid typographic foundation specifically tailored for screen-based motion.

lessons.what_is_taught: Operating text layers in After Effects: point text versus paragraph box text, character formatting panel, paragraph alignment options, font styling, vertical and horizontal transforms, and understanding text layer origins.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates cleanly aligned headline and subhead text layers with verified font weights and alignment.
lessons.why_it_matters: Proper text setup ensures animators apply predictable transformations across characters.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluent setup and formatting of After Effects text layers.

lessons.what_is_taught: The After Effects text animation engine: adding Text Animators, animating Position, Scale, Rotation, Opacity, Tracking, Character Offset, and combining multiple animated properties within a single animator.
lessons.what_learner_does: Adds a custom text animator combining upward Position offset, tracking expansion, and Opacity reveal.
lessons.why_it_matters: Text animators provide granular character-level control without splitting words into separate layers.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to configure and combine multiple text animator properties.

lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering the Range Selector: Start, End, and Offset properties; selecting by Characters, Characters Excluding Spaces, Words, or Lines; shape profiles (Square, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Smooth); and controlling easing within animators.
subtopics: Start, End and Offset percentage keys
Ease High and Ease Low adjustments
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures a Range Selector with Smooth shape and high Ease settings to animate a headline word by word.
lessons.why_it_matters: Range selectors allow smooth, wave-like character transitions that look sophisticated and organic.
lessons.expected_outcome: Complete command over Range Selectors for precise typographic animation.

lessons.what_is_taught: Structuring kinetic typography sequences: word-by-word timing, character cascade reveals, phrase transitions, emphasizing keywords through scale and colour changes, maintaining visual rhythm, and pacing text for effortless reading.
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates an 8-word commercial slogan with dynamic emphasis on key value words and seamless phrase transitions.
lessons.why_it_matters: Kinetic typography is a core commercial skill for social ads, music promos, and corporate manifestos.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to animate engaging, legible kinetic typography sequences.

lessons.what_is_taught: Aligning text animation to audio: placing timeline layer markers on speech syllables and musical beats, syncing word reveals with voiceover cadence, timing visual impact on percussive hits, and keeping speech clear.
subtopics: Syncing word entrances to voiceover syllables
lessons.what_learner_does: Times an animated text quote precisely to a voiceover audio track using timeline markers.
lessons.why_it_matters: Motion synchronized tightly to audio creates high viewer engagement and emotional impact.
lessons.expected_outcome: Precise synchronization of typographic animation with speech and musical cues.

lessons.what_is_taught: Animating brand identity: preparing vector logos in Illustrator, separating elements into layers, importing as editable compositions, designing purposeful entrance reveals, preserving brand proportions, and crafting clean rest settles.
lessons.what_learner_does: Prepares a multi-part vector logo, imports it into After Effects, and animates an original, elegant brand reveal.
lessons.why_it_matters: Logo reveals are among the most requested freelance motion graphics deliverables for digital brands.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to produce original, brand-respectful animated logo reveals.

lessons.what_is_taught: Designing broadcast and digital lower thirds: name and designation typographic hierarchy, animated graphic accent backgrounds, clean entrance and exit transitions, screen-safe positioning, and editable text layer architecture.
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs and animates a dual-line lower third with an animated accent bar and clean exit animation.
lessons.why_it_matters: Lower thirds are required for interviews, corporate videos, YouTube productions, and broadcast streams.
lessons.expected_outcome: Creation of professional, legible and easily editable lower thirds.

lessons.what_is_taught: Building animated title systems: title and subtitle hierarchy, geometric accents, intro/outro timing, consistent motion language, and structuring compositions so client editors can change text easily.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a modular chapter title sequence where replacement text updates seamlessly without adjusting keyframes.
lessons.why_it_matters: Reusable title packages allow agencies and clients to maintain consistent branding across series of videos.
lessons.expected_outcome: Competence in building robust, reusable animated title assets.

lessons.what_is_taught: Maintaining brand consistency in motion: establishing motion identity (snappy vs fluid, playful vs corporate), adhering to brand colour palettes and typography guidelines, avoiding off-brand effects, and audiovisual coherence.
lessons.what_learner_does: Evaluates a proposed animation against a brand style guide, adjusting motion curves and colours for alignment.
lessons.why_it_matters: Clients hire motion designers who understand brand identity, not just animation tricks.
lessons.expected_outcome: Understanding how to apply strict brand guidelines to motion-design workflows.

lessons.what_is_taught: Creating user-friendly editable After Effects project files: organized composition hierarchies, color-coded editable text layers, clear layer naming, quick colour-swap solids, and documented instructions for non-expert collaborators.
subtopics: Replacing text and asset layers cleanly
lessons.what_learner_does: Prepares a complete lower-third and title kit with editable text layers and a 1-page reuse guide.
lessons.why_it_matters: Deliverables that other team members can easily edit and customize have high commercial value.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to build and package reusable After Effects graphic templates.

lessons.what_is_taught: Auditing and refining the animation timeline: opening the Graph Editor to inspect velocity curves, checking movement hierarchy, verifying anticipation and settling, eliminating visual hitches, and ensuring effortless text reading.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for complete After Effects beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces animation principles and After Effects fundamentals before progressing to shape motion, kinetic typography and practical portfolio projects.

faq.question: What will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn timing, easing, keyframes, shape-layer animation, Trim Paths, kinetic typography, transitions, logo motion and basic motion-design production.

faq.question: What portfolio projects will I create?
faq.answer: You will create four focused deliverables: an 8–12-second kinetic typography sequence, a logo reveal, a reusable lower third or title animation, and a 15–20-second motion infographic or promotional sequence.

faq.question: Do I need Illustrator or Photoshop experience?
faq.answer: Basic design knowledge is helpful, but previous professional Illustrator or Photoshop experience is not required.

faq.question: Will I learn the Graph Editor?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn introductory easing and Graph Editor concepts to understand and refine animation timing. Advanced Graph Editor techniques belong to Course 69.

faq.question: Will I learn logo animation?
faq.answer: Yes. You will create a simple original logo reveal using basic motion techniques and editable After Effects layers.

faq.question: Will I learn kinetic typography?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum includes text animators, character/word animation, timing and typography hierarchy.

faq.question: Will I learn professional VFX and compositing?
faq.answer: No. This course focuses on foundational 2D motion design. Tracking, rotoscoping, advanced compositing and sophisticated motion systems are covered in Course 69.

faq.question: Can I use premade templates?
faq.answer: Templates may be studied as references, but assessed work must include meaningful original keyframe animation.

faq.question: Is Adobe software included in the fee?
faq.answer: Software licensing depends on Nova Skills' verified training arrangements. Do not claim paid Adobe subscriptions are included unless confirmed.

faq.question: Will I receive editable project files?
faq.answer: You will create and submit editable After Effects project files, organized assets and final video exports as part of your portfolio.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for graphic designers?
faq.answer: Yes. It is particularly suitable for graphic designers who want to add motion and animation skills to their existing design knowledge.

faq.question: What should I learn after this course?
faq.answer: Students seeking advanced motion graphics, tracking, compositing and reusable professional templates may progress to Course 69.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course lasts five weeks, includes 40 guided learning hours and has a listed fee of ₹5,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
